correctness.rationale: On ℤ, the ordinary heat-kernel difference d_j(u)=p₁(u,j)−p₁(u,j+1) solves a positive irreducible tridiagonal system; off-diagonal positive paths imply d_j(u)>0. For 0<s<1, Bochner positive-stable subordination integrates these strictly decreasing kernels at positive times, giving symmetric strictly unimodal p_s∈ℓ¹. Therefore the ∞→∞ forward-difference norm telescopes to 2p_s(t,0), with the same sign-step extremizer. For 0<a<b≤1, the CDF difference g(y)=F(U^a;y)−F(U^b;y) has the strict sign − on 0<y<1 and + on 1<y<4^b. Integrating by parts yields Δp=t∫e^(−ty)g(y)dy. H=e^tΔp/t has H′=−∫(y−1)e^(−t(y−1))g(y)dy<0; H(0)=m(b)−m(a)>0 from strict convexity of m(s)=E(U^s), m′(0)=E log U=0; H→−∞ from the strictly negative y<1 interval. There is one simple positive zero and the stated reversal. Beta identity and Laplace saddle rescaling give displayed short- and long-time coefficients. Analytic positivity and derivative signs establish all times/orders; finite evaluations do not.
residual_risks: The proof uses stable subordination only for 0<s≤1; does not extend unimodality to s>1.
Strict simple crossing concerns ℓ∞→ℓ∞ norm of D e^(−tL^s), not ℓ¹→ℓ∞ gradient kernel peaks.

value.rationale: Identifies the exact worst-case rough-input smoothing norm for every order with one extremizer, and proves a surprising global reversal: no fractional power dominates another in sharp gradient smoothing at every time. This is not a routine rate estimate; the strict one-crossing classification removes ambiguity among a continuum of diffusion orders on a natural lattice model.
